subject: Marketplace connector / Partner paper — pass-through liability & invoicing routing
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudforge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Marketplace connector - partner paper / MSA redlines (pass-through)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are the partner paper redlines from our procurement team — the primary open item for us is the pass-through clause in Section 6 (liability and tax routing) and the invoicing flow for marketplace-referred customers.

High-level asks:
- We need Redwood to accept a pass-through carveout for marketplace-fee allocation (CloudForge to remit marketplace fees directly to the marketplace; Redwood to invoice net usage).
- We also want an explicit statement that CloudForge can require an escrow/backstop for reseller settlements in certain territories.
- Audit rights: limited to records relevant to marketplace invoicing for 24 months.

We understand this may touch the MSA + Order Form combination — we can be flexible if we can get the language carved into an addendum. Attached: CloudForge_PassThrough_Redlines.pdf (redline).

Can you confirm next steps and expected timeline for internal legal review? We have a billing window target of EOY for Launch.

Best,
Emily Park
Senior Procurement Manager
CloudForge Inc.
procurement@cloudforge.com
Attachment: CloudForge_PassThrough_Redlines.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <procurement@cloudforge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace connector - partner paper / MSA redlines (pass-through)

Hi Emily — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Looping in legal (Kimberly) and Channel (Marissa) to triage.

We can move quickly on this, but there are three points we need to reconcile internally before we propose an addendum:
1) Pass-through carveout: we need clarity on whether CloudForge wants Redwood to waive any recovery right against marketplace fees or simply accept a routing convention on the invoice. The former is a broader indemnity ask.
2) Escrow/backstop: operationally this impacts how orders are reconciled and how refunds are handled — we need Finance ops input.
3) Audit scope: 24 months is reasonable; we need to confirm confidentiality/non-disclosure boundaries.

Kimberly and Marissa — can you take point on redline review? Karthik, can you prep the deal-specific billing flow (who pays marketplace fee, who invoices customer, and a failover if the marketplace rejects settlement)?

Emily — target for us is to get an internal position by end of day Thursday (12/3) and come back with a proposed partner addendum that preserves Redwood's MSA protections while giving CloudForge the invoicing certainty. Would a 13:00 PT call on Friday work for you if we need to talk through the compromise language?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive — Partnerships
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T15:28:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: CloudForge redlines — quick legal take (draft comments attached)

Team — quick legal read attached (RF_legal_comments.docx). High-level:
- Pass-through carveout: counter-propose language that makes routing operational ("marketplace fees will be reflected as a passthrough on invoices where applicable") but preserves Redwood's right to collect and offset. Explicit waiver of recovery against Redwood is a no from Legal unless priced/insured.
- Escrow/backstop: we can accept a limited settlement hold in higher-risk APAC territories only, with caps and sunset (propose 12 months post-launch).
- Audit rights: agree 24 months, but audits must be narrowly scoped, at reasonable intervals, and under NDA; Redwood can require redaction for customer-identifying info.

I prepared two sample clauses in the attached docx: (A) conservative Redwood-friendly addendum and (B) a compromise draft that trades a limited settlement hold for a short fee premium (we should ask Sales if pricing is an option).

Next steps: Jordan — do you want me to send the compromise draft to Emily or hand it to Channel to negotiate commercial terms first?

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: RF_legal_comments.docx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <procurement@cloudforge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace connector - partner paper / MSA redlines (pass-through)

Hi Emily — we reviewed your redlines with Legal and Channel. Attached is a proposed addendum (Redwood_Response_Redlines.pdf) that aims to:
- Accept marketplace invoicing routing ("net of marketplace fees") as an operational default,
- Preserve Redwood's collection and offset rights if marketplace settlement fails,
- Limit escrow/backstop to specific APAC territories with a 12-month sunset, and
- Agree to a 24-month limited-scope audit right under NDA.

We tried to keep the language narrowly tailored so it does not modify the core MSA indemnities. If CloudForge needs Redwood to waive recovery rights entirely, we would need to escalate to Commercial Leadership and review pricing impact.

Please see attached and let me know where you'd like to converge. If helpful, I'm available for a 13:00 PT call Friday to walk through the clauses and the billing flow.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive — Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Response_Redlines.pdf

From: Emily Park <procurement@cloudforge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lewis <anna.lewis@legalpartners.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace connector - partner paper / MSA redlines (pass-through)

Jordan — thanks for the quick review and the addendum draft. We reviewed internally and appreciate the compromise. Two outstanding items before we can sign off:
1) Recovery waiver: CloudForge procurement cannot accept a unilateral right for Redwood to offset marketplace collections without a carveout for material settlement failures. We have proposed a narrow "no recovery for marketplace-collected fees" line in our redlines — can Redwood accept a limited remedy cap (e.g., equal to marketplace fees collected in the prior quarter) instead of full waiver?
2) Escrow mechanics: we need more detail on how the proposed APAC settlement hold would operate operationally (timing, triggers, who holds the funds). Can you ask Finance to provide a short ops note?

Cc'ing our counsel (Anna Lewis) so she can review the compromise language for audit and escrow. If acceptable, we'd like to schedule the Friday 13:00 PT call to finalize language and confirm invoicing flow.

Best,
Emily Park
Senior Procurement Manager
CloudForge Inc.
Attachment: CloudForge_Final_Questions.txt
